t: The Angevin Charles I rebuilt royal power after the Árpád line died out in 1301, ruling from Visegrád and later Buda.
Gold from its mines made Hungary Europe's leading producer of precious metals and its florin a standard coin.
Matthias Corvinus made it a Renaissance power, but magnate rule followed and the Ottomans crushed it at Mohács in 1526.
dyk: The Bibliotheca Corviniana of Matthias Corvinus was one of the largest libraries of Renaissance Europe; over two hundred of its volumes survive in collections across the world.
ev: Andrew III dies, ending the Árpád dynasty
Charles I is crowned with the Holy Crown at Székesfehérvár
Louis I also becomes king of Poland
Sigismund's crusade is destroyed at the Battle of Nicopolis
John Hunyadi breaks the Ottoman siege of Belgrade
The peasant revolt of György Dózsa is crushed
Suleiman the Magnificent defeats the Hungarians at Mohács; Louis II dies

f.successor: Kingdom of Hungary (1526-1867); Eastern Hungarian Kingdom; Ottoman Empire
